arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Mashburn stated the Tribe contracted for off-reservation construction.
Mr. Coleman argued the contract waived immunity for arbitration.
Mr. Garre cited precedent recognizing tribal sovereign immunity.
Mr. Minnis argued an arbitration clause is not a waiver.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: C & L Enterprises built a roof for the Potawatomi Tribe off-reservation. The contract included an arbitration clause. The parties disputed the award. C & L Enterprises sued in state court to confirm the award. The Tribe argued sovereign immunity blocked the suit. The lower court ruled against the Tribe. C & L Enterprises won that lower-court action.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Tribes face state court suits over commercial contracts. Clear waiver rules protect tribal sovereignty. Businesses need reliable dispute resolution mechanisms. This case defines the scope of tribal immunity.
